verdict.rationale: Clerk publishes its own migration guide covering Basic Export/Import and Trickle migration strategies. It also provides an open-source tool that imports users from a JSON or CSV file through the Backend API and respects rate limits. The no-forced-reset part of the story is not evidenced: nothing says password hashes are imported or that users keep their existing passwords, and no guide is shown for a specific competing provider. Missing for 10: documented password-hash import or preservation without resets, provider-specific migration guides (e.g. from Auth0 or Firebase), and independent or hands-on corroboration of a migration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can follow vendor-maintained migration guides or tooling for moving off a competing auth provider without forcing password resets

citations.quote: To aid in basic migrations, Clerk provides an open-source tool that takes a JSON or CSV file as input, containing a list of users, and creates a user in Clerk using the Backend API
There are typically two main strategies for migrating your existing user management from a different platform into Clerk: Basic Export / Import, Trickle migration
